findings: The hero title "Uncle Joey's of Merrimack" is overlapped by the tagline, and a popup covers the page on load.
The menu is a single 3600px image of the printed menu, so it can't be read on a phone, searched or linked to.
The Order Online button carries copied Google Ads tracking parameters (utm_source=PaidGoogle, gclid=…).
Navigation has an empty first button; every nav item only scrolls the same page.
The hours block ends with a stray "Closed" line that doesn't name a day (it means Monday).
The only real photos on the site are the logo and one cheese pizza; Slice's item photos are stock catalog images, so we didn't use them.
questions: Printed-menu prices are lower than Slice (Slice adds a markup: cheese pie $13.99 online vs $11.99/$15.99 in store). Should the website show in-store prices?
Two pizzas are on Slice but not the printed menu (The Big Mac, The Bee Sting). Are they current?
Can we photograph the shop? One real pie photo isn't enough for the site; a shoot of Chick Stix, the Supremo, a calzone and the family would carry the whole design.
Catering: the catering menu image shows half/full tray prices (Caesar $40/$60, Chick Stix $60/$94, etc.). Do you want a catering section with those?
Do you want the Nashua shop linked from this site, or kept fully separate?
Is the "Closed" line on the current site meant to be Monday?
